 Interim CEO Colette Kress on Nvidia earnings, revenue growth estimates, and hyperscaler demand
 2 min read NVDA Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress said hyperscalers are “feverishly looking for more focus in the compute that we have available” as the company just reported earnings. 
 The chipmaker raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth forecast to 75% from the previous 70% guidance, citing continuous demand for the company's compute infrastructure and agentic AI solutions. 
 The announcement came during an interview with CNBC's Jim Cramer following Nvidia's Q3 earnings report, marking Kress's first public comments since founder Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO last week. 
 Kress attributed the upgraded outlook to both surging customer interest and improved supply chain coordination. She said customer demand has only intensified in recent weeks, with some looking to accelerate purchases into the early part of the fiscal year. 
 Addressing concerns about potential brain drain following Huang's departure, Kress emphasized employee dedication and leadership continuity. 
 "The company has been built under the perspective that the employees look at Nvidia NVDA as their life's work. And many of them have been here for many decades," she said in an interview with CNBC. 
 The board has determined it will not reinstate Huang in any capacity, with Kress stating the company's focus remains on growing the business for employees, customers, and shareholders. 
 On capital allocation, Kress announced Nvidia NVDA is increasing its stock repurchase authorization by more than $150B, bringing the total buyback program to $277B through the end of 2027. 
 The company also clarified its financial exposure, stating actual guarantees stand at approximately $118B—far below the $530B figure cited by some analysts—with the largest commitment being a land, power, and shell backstop for a 4.5-gigawatt data center facility in Portsmouth. 
 Kress dismissed suggestions that hyperscalers are abandoning Nvidia for competitors or in-house chip solutions. 
 "If we want to think about where we are with our hyperscalers, they are the ones that are right now feverishly looking for more focus in terms of the compute that we have available," she said. 
 Regarding China exposure, Kress noted that shipments to the country represent approximately 10% of revenue, consisting primarily of gaming, automotive, and workstation products, and confirmed Nvidia NVDA has stopped shipping H200 chips entirely. 
 The interim CEO confirmed that financing partnerships with Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and Apollo for the two-way compute market project will continue. 
 "Those financing funds are very important to us," Kress said, adding that the partnerships help companies near investment grade access capital while establishing Nvidia's NVDA systems as a distinct asset class with unmatched durability and fungibility.
